newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 9.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Finance Ministry has prepared a new tariff structure for next year.

- The parliament appears optimistic about the budget for 1997. The chairman of the budget committee, Jozef Wagner believes that the new budget will be accepted; a few modifications are possible, but not necessary.
- Small business markets are showing record sales before Christmas. The increase is most probably caused by more appealing offers and more representatives of small businesses.

- Low defence expenses in the budget are jeopardising the Czech Republic's chances of joining NATO. The Minister of Defense, Miloslav Vyborny proposed an increase of about 32 billion crowns for next year.

- Plzensky Prazdroj brewery expects record beer sales this year covering about 22 per cent of the domestic market, five per cent more than last year. The company's goal for 1997 is to control up to 40 per cent of domestic sales.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - President Vaclav Havel managed to get up and breathe without the help of a breathing machine twice yesterday, although on Thursday doctors had to help his breathing with tubes going straight to his windpipe. Doctors predict that Havel will be connected to a ventilator for at least five more days.

- Railway workers, who during their last strike caused the resignation of the general director of Czech Railways and an end to the railway reconstruction project, are prepared to strike again. They are apparently not happy with the current management as well and consider it to be a critical situation.

PRAVO - Vladimir Dlouhy, the Minister of Industry and Trade, on a three day official visit in China, stated in a meeting with journalists in Beijing that the Czech trade deficit will be between 160 and 170 billion crowns this year.
- According to a survey done by the IVVM opinion poll agency Ceska Televize has the most objective news reports, followed by TV Nova and Premiera TV.
